newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria eyes foreign advice to restructure firms.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria eyes foreign advice to restructure firms.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to seek foreign consultants for restructuring its state firms to bring them closer to international production and marketing standards, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said on Wednesday.

"We should seek foreign consultants not only for our big privatisation projects but also for restructuring state enterprises if we want an efficient structural reform," Bozhkov told a seminar on selection criteria for sell-off consultants.
Bozhkov said Bulgaria's tobacco industry, a traditional source of export revenue, should be restructured through foreign advice to boost its competitiveness on world markets.
The government approved this month a restructuring programme for the state tobacco monopolist Bulgartabac Holding to boost management and marketing efficiency.
"Foreign expertise could also be useful in liquidation of state loss-making enterprises which is a vital part of the structural reform," said Bozhkov.

A new reformist government that took office in May has said that Bulgaria will call tenders for consultants in the privatisation of 30 large companies such as the state carrier Balkan Airlines, the Neftochim oil refinery and three shipyards.

The deadline for potential bidders at the tenders for 29 of the companies on the list expires on July 28, said Alexander Sabotinov, executive director of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency that handles major sell-offs.

Consultant services are to be paid for through the European Union's Phare programme, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and success fees deducted from the total privatisation proceeds.

Last week the government approved draft amendments to the Privatisation Law, raising to 10 percent from seven percent the share of privatisation proceeds that could be used for covering expenses in the sell-offs, including consultant fees.

"This will make sell-offs more attractive to prospective major consultants and will provide us more room for selection, allowing us to seek better terms at the sell-offs," said Bozhkov. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
